record.paper_title: Confinement of color: open problems and perspectives.
record.context_brief: Operational confinement criterion in full QCD
record.original_question: In full QCD with dynamical quarks, what operational definition or order parameter should be used to distinguish the confined phase from the deconfined phase? The usual Polyakov-line criterion works in the quenched theory because the Z_3 center symmetry is exact there, but with dynamical quarks that symmetry is explicitly broken and the confining string can break through quark-pair creation, so neither the Polyakov loop nor the chiral condensate is generically an exact order parameter at nonzero quark mass.

evidence.quote: The real problem, both on the lattice and in experiment, is to give an operational definition of confined and deconfined.

In the presence of dynamical quarks the symmetry Z3 is explicitly broken and the string breaks at large enough distances converting the energy into the formation of quark pairs. No clear criterion exists to define confined and deconfined.
At generic values of m neither < L > nor < ψψ¯ > are order parameters.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) formulated as an SU(3) lattice gauge theory with N_f flavors of dynamical quarks of nonzero mass m. In the pure-gauge (quenched) limit, the theory has an exact global Z_3 center symmetry, and the expectation value of the Polyakov loop ⟨L⟩ serves as an exact order parameter distinguishing the confined phase (⟨L⟩ = 0) from the deconfined phase (⟨L⟩ ≠ 0). Likewise, in the chiral limit m → 0 the quark condensate ⟨ψ̄ψ⟩ is an exact order parameter for chiral symmetry breaking. For generic finite quark mass 0 < m < ∞, however, the Z_3 center symmetry is explicitly broken by the quark determinant (so the static color string can break via dynamical quark–antiquark pair creation and ⟨L⟩ ≠ 0 everywhere), while chiral symmetry is also explicitly broken (so ⟨ψ̄ψ⟩ ≠ 0 everywhere). Provide an operational definition, or a local/non-local order parameter, that gauge-invariantly and unambiguously distinguishes a "confined" phase from a "deconfined" phase of full QCD with dynamical quarks at generic m, both at zero and at finite temperature, in a manner that (i) reduces to the standard Polyakov-loop criterion in the quenched limit, (ii) can in principle be measured on the lattice and in experiment, and (iii) is sharp (i.e., associated with a genuine non-analyticity or with a well-defined topological/algebraic invariant) rather than a crossover.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of an exact operational order parameter for color confinement in full QCD with dynamical quarks remains an open problem. Standard references (lattice QCD reviews, the Clay Millennium Problem on Yang-Mills mass gap, and recent surveys on "different faces of confinement") confirm that neither the Polyakov loop nor the chiral condensate is an order parameter at generic finite quark mass, and that the transition from low to high temperature in full QCD is generally a crossover. No universally accepted sharp criterion has been established.

status_evidence.title: open problem of confinement -- references in nLab
status_evidence.snippet: The quark confinement conjecture is experimentally well tested, but mathematically still unproven.
status_evidence.claim: Confinement in full QCD remains mathematically unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Different faces of confinement
status_evidence.snippet: Review discussing the multiple, non-equivalent criteria proposed for confinement and their limitations in the presence of dynamical quarks.
status_evidence.claim: No single agreed operational order parameter exists for confinement with dynamical quarks.

status_evidence.title: Mechanism of quark confinement in QCD
status_evidence.snippet: A basic understanding of the mechanism of color confinement and its relation to chiral symmetry breaking in QCD has remained an unsolved problem.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization of QCD confinement is listed as an open problem.
